Chapter 155: 0152 The Spirit of the Internet is Sharing (Bonus chapter for Alliance Leader Yu Xian Qi Tian)

Having the same gameplay is not considered plagiarism.

As long as the code, art, sound effects, and text weren't too similar, anyone could imitate *Sanguosha* and *Happy Farm*.

There was no legal risk whatsoever.

If Tencent wanted to copy them, so be it. Chen Guilang had launched *Happy Farm* with only two core objectives:

First, to increase user activity on the Xiaonei Network.

Second, to drive traffic to the newly created Youke Interactive Entertainment Platform.

Several days later, Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun finally met with Chen Guilang again.

Chen Guilang invited them to look at the backend data.

Lin Dongliang leaned over the computer. "It's only been a few days. How are the registered users already approaching 1.5 million?"

Fu Jixun said, "No matter how popular *Happy Farm* is, it couldn't have achieved this, could it?"

Chen Guilang smiled. "The real-name registration system for all university BBS forums has been fully implemented."

The implementation of the real-name registration system for university BBS forums did not happen on the same day.

The Ministry of Education had only given a deadline and initiated the rectifications in early March.

Some universities were very thorough, banning off-campus IP logins and even preventing anonymous browsing, like Peking University.

Other universities were more lenient, prohibiting off-campus IPs from posting and registering. But accounts registered previously could still log in and browse posts, like Shanghai Jiao Tong University.

During the final phase of the rectification, the BBS forums of major universities were filled with farewell messages. Taking Qinghua's BBS as an example, the number of daily active users plummeted to just three or four thousand.

Whether you called it a rebellious mentality or a temporary discomfort, many university students stopped using BBS forums for a short period. And the Xiaonei Network became their first-choice "refuge"!

It just so happened that the Xiaonei Network was continuously running promotions and upgrading its servers and bandwidth, very smoothly accommodating and retaining these people.

Even the Zhanzuo Network managed to get a piece of the pie, with its registered users reaching over 36,000.

By the way, due to the difficulty of controlling online rumors and the outrageous audacity of certain elements, in three months, even QQ group owners would be required to register with their real names!

Next would be the real-name registration system for blogs the following year, requiring all bloggers to register with their real names.

This trend of real-name registration finally ceased when the internet real-name registration legislation failed to pass in 2008. The era of revelry for online public intellectuals also arrived along with it...

Can you imagine a group of famous bloggers, media outlets, and corporations coordinating on Weibo to repeatedly insult the martyrs from our textbooks? It was as absurd as it could get.

Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun said no more, just staring at the other data on the Xiaonei Network's backend.

Chen Guilang said, "According to last year's 'National Education Development Statistics Bulletin' from the Ministry of Education, in 2004, there were approximately 9.95 million undergraduate students, 3.39 million junior college students, 22.2 million high school students, and 14.09 million vocational high school students. A total of 49.63 million people!"

"Our next step is to open up registration for high school and vocational high school students."

"Looking at the data longitudinally over the past few years, the scale of these student groups has been continuously growing. This year, the number of undergraduate students will definitely break 10 million, and the total number of the above student groups will certainly exceed 50 million."

"Oh, and I haven't even included Master's and PhD students. Last year, there were about 3.09 million Master's students and about 560,000 PhD students. They are also users of the Xiaonei Network."

Chen Guilang pointed at the computer and said, "The current 1.5 million registered users don't even amount to a fraction of the total. As the base of registered users expands, the natural rate of viral growth will become faster and faster. An increase of 10,000 users a day is still a conservative estimate. As long as we maintain user stickiness, an increase of 50,000 users a day is possible."

Fu Jixun nitpicked, "The more users there are, the higher the operational cost for the Xiaonei Network, and your profitability remains an issue. QQ has enough users and high enough stickiness, right? More than half of its profits come from wireless value-added services on Mobile QQ."

Lin Dongliang also said, "The country is tightening its policies on wireless value-added services, so it will be difficult to rely on that for long-term profit. That's why Tencent's stock price has been very low, and now they have to raise funds to buy back their own stock. If you can't find a monetization point for the Xiaonei Network, Series B financing and a future IPO will be very difficult to execute."

Chen Guilang smiled. "Gentlemen, things develop and move forward, and China's development speed has always been very fast. A few years ago, the internet bubble burst, and over 90% of internet companies went bankrupt. Everyone thought it was the end of the world, but didn't wireless value-added services suddenly appear and save a large number of Chinese companies?"

"When wireless value-added services are gone, more ways to make money will emerge. Because the number of netizens is increasing and internet speeds are getting faster, there's a strong demand for monetization. The market demand is there, and it will automatically select the best method. In this process, some companies will die, but it definitely won't be me!"

"The Xiaonei Network is already accepting ads, and they are high-quality ads for things like electronics, because all my users here are high-quality users. Although *Happy Farm* won't earn too much money, it will definitely be profitable to some extent. In the coming year, my goal is to achieve break-even."

Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun exchanged a glance.

"Then let's talk about the valuation," Lin Dongliang said.

Chen Guilang interrupted, "Let's not talk about valuation first. Let's talk about how much equity you two want."

Lin Dongliang said, "IDG wants 15%."

Fu Jixun said, "DFJ wants 12%."

"That's too much, it's impossible. I need to leave enough room for Series B financing," Chen Guilang shook his head. "And taking 27% from me in Series A is forcing me to adopt a dual-class share structure. Hong Kong doesn't allow listings with a dual-class share structure, so I'd have to go to the US, and the US also reviews dual-class shares very strictly. By doing this, you're not just screwing me over, you're screwing yourselves over too!"

Lin Dongliang asked, "How much are you willing to give?"

"18% at most," Chen Guilang said.

Fu Jixun said, "We need to discuss this further."

"Be my guest." Chen Guilang was planning to stall for time anyway.

Meanwhile, on the Flash Empire Baidu Tieba, a large number of ad posts appeared: Youke Interactive Entertainment's Call for Talent is out!

Although the bar moderator reacted quickly, deleting them as soon as they appeared, the ad posts kept popping up endlessly.

In the end, it angered the majority of the bar's members, who questioned the moderator one after another about why he was deleting these posts.

Why delete them?

Because Youke Interactive Entertainment could potentially poach users from Flash Empire!

But the members didn't care about the business consequences; they were all contributing out of passion. Now there was another website waiting for them to contribute, and the moderator was actually stopping them from showing their love.

How despicable.

The issue escalated, and the moderator was flamed so badly he resigned directly.

The ad posts for Youke Interactive Entertainment could finally appear openly again, their numbers now controlled to avoid being annoying.

Call for Talent: Sincerely inviting Flash masters to create games and upload them to Youke Interactive Entertainment. Creators will be paid in site currency based on the number and duration of player sessions. The site currency can be converted into RMB and paid to the creator each quarter, and can also be used to purchase in-game items for other Youke games.

There was no other way. These kinds of small Flash games couldn't sell any in-game items at all. The only way to profit was by increasing website traffic, which would attract advertisers, and then earn money from advertising.

However, the production cost of small Flash games was very low. A relatively simple one could be made for just a few hundred yuan, and it didn't require the creator's skills to be particularly brilliant.

If the creator was a multi-talented individual, there might be no production cost at all, just a bit more time invested.

Tian Rui was a Flasher, currently a student at the Communication University of China, and a long-time member of Flash Empire.

Tian Rui asked in a QQ group, "Who's going to post small games on Youke Interactive Entertainment?"

"I want to give it a try. I heard you can convert site currency into RMB every quarter."

"Anyone here know about law? Go check out Youke's user agreement."

"I've read it. It's pretty legitimate. The copyright remains in our own hands. If Youke wants to buy it out, they'll sign a separate supplementary agreement. However, if you upload it to Youke, it's automatically assumed that Youke has the right of first refusal to purchase the copyright."
